vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news — this is something you (or almost any web developer) can fix yourself in a few minutes. Here's how to check and open it up:

## 1. Check what's currently blocking you
Visit `yoursite.com/robots.txt` in a browser. If you're blocking AI crawlers, you'll see something like "User-agent: GPTBot / Disallow: /" or a blanket rule like `User-agent: * / Disallow: /` that blocks everything - including all AI crawlers.

You can also use a free automated checker instead of reading it manually:
- **MRS Digital's AI Crawler Access Checker** — allows you to see whether popular AI crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot can reach your website's pages.
- **365i AI Crawler Checker** — tests 14 AI bots against your robots.txt and your live server, checks for noindex and nosnippet, then writes a fix message for your hosting company.
- **LLM Pulse Robots.txt Checker** — shows you exactly which AI and search crawlers you allow or block, line by line.
- **RankPrompt**, **SEOcrawl**, and similar free tools do the same thing — paste your URL and get a bot-by-bot report.

These tools require no login and just need your domain name.

## 2. Who can actually fix it
- **You, if you manage your own site** (WordPress, Shopify, Squarespace, custom code): editing robots.txt is simple text editing.
- **Your web developer or webmaster** if someone else built/manages the site.
- **Your hosting company** — some hosts or security plugins (Wordfence, Sucuri, Cloudflare) add bot-blocking rules you may not see in robots.txt itself. Some SEO and security plugins add AI bot blocks as a default setting, and some hosts ship a managed robots.txt template with AI crawlers pre-blocked. Notably, since July 1, 2025, Cloudflare blocks AI bots by default on every new domain via its "AI Scrapers and Crawlers" managed rule, even if your robots.txt says Allow — so if you're on Cloudflare, check that setting too.

## 3. How to open it up
Edit (or create) your robots.txt file in your site's root directory and add Allow rules for the major AI assistant crawlers:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

User-agent: *
Allow: /
```

If you use a CDN like Cloudflare or Fastly, make sure the CDN isn't adding its own bot-blocking rules on top of your robots.txt.

## 4. Verify the fix worked
- Re-visit `yoursite.com/robots.txt` to confirm the new rules are live.
- Re-run one of the free checker tools above.
- You can also inspect your server/CDN logs and check the HTTP response codes — 200 means success, 403 means still blocked.

If you tell me your website platform (WordPress, Squarespace, Shopify, custom site, etc.) or host (Cloudflare, GoDaddy, etc.), I can give you exact click-by-click steps for your setup.
